patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Davis is a 65-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes but no known epilepsy who presents with altered mental status. His wife reports that he was watching television when he had a brief episode of shaking lasting about 30 seconds approximately 45 minutes ago. He did not fall. After the shaking he seemed confused and has remained confused since — he is saying nonsensical things and is disoriented. She thought he would recover but he has been persistently confused for 45 minutes. He has never had a seizure before. She denies any headache, fever, or focal weakness preceding the episode. He has had no recent illnesses. He was at his baseline this morning. He has no substance use except moderate alcohol. His blood glucose at home was 84 mg/dL when she checked it during the episode, ruling out hypoglycemia. On arrival he is awake but confused and disoriented, unable to follow complex commands. EEG was immediately performed.
